bindings.label: One-year history of persistent erythematous papules and infiltrative plaques on the nose and upper jaw

35-year-old Chinese female presented on March 7, 2018 with a one-year history of lesions; initially a rice-grain-sized hard nodule appeared on the right alar part of the nose, painless and itchy, without obvious triggers; over time the lesions increased in size, became thick, and spread across the entire nose, with infiltrating plaques also developing on the upper jaw
Past and family history showed no similar diseases in the family; since illness onset, urine, stool, and weight remained normal
Skin examination revealed diffuse erythematous papules, infiltrations, and hypertrophic plaques on the entire nose and upper jaw, with a smooth surface

Dermoscopy showed a bright red background with diffuse telangiectasia but no obvious keratinized hair follicle structures; laboratory tests for antinuclear antibody, anti-dsDNA antibody, anti-Ro, anti-La, and Borrelia, as well as direct immunofluorescence serology, were negative; blood and urine routine, liver and kidney function, chest X-ray, and ECG showed no obvious abnormalities

Maxillary CT plain scan with enhancement revealed (1) a soft tissue nodule in the right soft palate, multiple enlarged lymph nodes in both necks, and thickening and enhancement of nasal soft tissue; (2) right frontal sinus and ethmoid sinusitis
Facial granulomatous disease
Lymphoproliferative disorder
Cutaneous autoimmune disease
Granulomatous rosacea
Skin biopsy shows no granulomas
Skin biopsy shows dense perivascular and periadnexal CD4+ T-cell infiltrate
Immunohistochemistry is positive for CD20, CD43, CD68, and CD1a
Ki-67 proliferation index is 10%
PAS, AFB, CD123, CD56, and GB stains are negative
TCR gene rearrangement analysis shows no clonal peaks
Reactive pseudolymphoma/cutaneous lymphoid hyperplasia
Sinonasal and lymph node biopsy and systemic lymphoma staging have not yet been performed
Jessner lymphocytic infiltration of the skin (T-cell cutaneous pseudolymphoma)
Jessner lymphocytic infiltration of the skin (T-cell cutaneous pseudolymphoma)
Lymphocytoma cutis (B-cell cutaneous pseudolymphoma)
Reactive cutaneous lymphoid hyperplasia secondary to chronic sinonasal/ethmoidal inflammation
Idiopathic cutaneous lymphoid hyperplasia (no identifiable trigger)
